Engine

What every world gets before a line of game code, area by area. Open one to read how it works and what it means for the game.

read →
Multiplayer & rooms

Every Spawn world is multiplayer out of the box: rooms, the 64-player place view, who simulates what, and how a referee keeps a match fair.

read →
Places & portals

A world is one game with many places: a town, a dungeon, an arena. Doors between them, instanced copies, and portals to other creators' worlds.

read →
Terrain & ground

Rolling heightmap hills, diggable voxel blocks, or no terrain at all: the ground, its materials, and the seas, lakes, rivers and paths marked on it.

read →
Objects, shapes & templates

Everything you see is an object: built-in shapes, scripted geometry, models, lights, signs, children and templates that stamp out fifty goblins from one.

read →
Physics & collision

Static walls, tumbling crates, moving lifts, walking characters, trigger zones, pass-through teams, raycasts, joints and ragdolls.

read →
Scripts, hooks & the sim

How a game's rules are written: behaviors, the hooks the engine calls, events, timers, and sim.js, the 30 Hz referee.

read →
State, saves & SQL

Where a game remembers things: the player's own save, room and object state, scratch space, and a world-wide SQL database for all-time boards.

read →
HUD & screens

How the screen over the game works: ui.js returns HTML each time state moves, buttons send actions, and panels can hang on objects in the world.

read →
Sound & music

Sounds named into being, spatial audio on objects, one-shot playSound, and the shared jukebox for music: how a game is heard.

read →
Light, sky, looks & effects

Sky, sun, fog and time of day, lights on objects, whole-screen looks, and the particle effects grammar for fire, dust and impacts.

read →
Cameras

A camera is a script: third-person orbits, first-person, top-down and cinematic shots, and how the camera reads the player's look.

read →
Controls, phones & devices

Declaring axes and actions, reading them in onInput, and how phones, gamepads and headsets get controls without extra work.

read →
Characters & animation

Player bodies, avatars, the 61-clip humanoid library, animation channels, and scripted creatures with their own skeletons.

read →
NPC minds & AI jobs

How NPCs think: one manager stepping a crowd, hearing noise, pathfinding, and off-loop jobs that call AI text models.

read →
Making art, sound & models

Where everything seen and heard comes from: scripted geometry, Blender models, painted pictures, seamless textures, uploads and named sounds.

read →
Publishing, players & social

Posting a game, rooms and matchmaking, singleplayer vs multiplayer, saves, parties, guilds and what Spawn handles for every player.

read →
Performance & scale

Holding 60fps on phones: what the engine does for you, where your scripts cost, the 500 m simulation radius, and how to measure.
